What is SLP Transitions​?

You're more than just a clinician.

SLP Transitions helps you find fulfilling work, with or without going back to school.

You went into SLP to help others, make a decent living, and have some flexibility. But unfortunately, a career that seems rewarding on paper can be burnout central "in the field."

At SLP Transitions, I interview successful career changers and entrepreneurs who made the leap from SLP to adjacent or seemingly unrelated fields. I share the stories behind their transition, with key takeaways you can apply to your own path. In each interview, I ask how they got started, how they managed their mindset, how they made themselves marketable, and how they enjoy their work today.

The stories are inspiring and also provide specific advice and insight into starting transitioning to a new career. By sharing these stories, I want to help other SLPs get started on the right foot.

The move usually takes longer than people expect, and it goes faster with a plan. Subscribe to get the interviews and guides in your inbox.

Who runs this site?

My name is James Berges. I spent over three years as an SLP in schools, private practice, and some acute and outpatient. I liked the 1-1 work with students and clients. What sent me looking outside the field was the red tape, the never-ending paperwork, and caseloads I had no control over.

I wanted to own my time, and full-time clinical work didn't allow that. I also noticed I got into a flow state doing creative and entrepreneurial work in a way I never quite did writing reports. So I started taking freelance marketing clients on the side, kept a few private SLP clients through the transition, and built it up until I could leave.

That freelance work is what got me here: I'm now full-time at Osmind, doing content strategy and marketing for software and research at the frontier of mental health treatment. It's a role I love, and it's the same shape as the transitions I write about on this site: a clinical background plus skills built on the side, put to work somewhere the clinical background is an asset rather than a requirement.

I still don't have all the answers, and I'm still experimenting. Let's support each other along the way.

You can learn about my other websites, apps, and marketing projects/ view my portfolio here.

I also co-host Xceptional Leaders, a podcast of conversations with entrepreneurs and advocates in the disability space — 190+ episodes, and once featured in Forbes.

I also share updates on the SLP Transitions Instagram!

How do I get my Story featured on SLP Transitions?

I'm always looking for people to interview. The story form walks you through it: where you worked, what you do now, how long the move took and what changed on your résumé. It comes straight to me, and nothing is published until you've seen the draft.

Share your story →

Advertise with us!

If you're interested at all in advertising on our website or newsletter, contact us here.

Affiliate Link Disclosure

Some of our future content may contain affiliate links, which means we may receive a commission if you click a link and purchase something that we have recommended.

While clicking these links won't cost you any extra money, they will help us keep this site up and running AND keep it free of annoying ads! Thank you for your support!
